prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and for showing how reallocation across firms shapes exporting, foreign investment and the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed. In round 1 I put B021 first. After the exchange I now put B038 first, with Melitz and Helpman. The reason is that I applied one standard to my own candidate that I had applied to the others. The chair asked whether theory-led or weakly identified work should meet the same bar as microdata-based work. On that question B021 is exposed in two ways I stated myself: parts of the cross-country evidence on constitutions and electoral rules rest on weaker causal designs, and the 2024 institutions prize, which I presented, sits close enough that the committee may read the two as one theme. B038 meets the bar better. Melitz (2003) and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple analysis of exporting versus foreign investment moved trade analysis from industries to firms. The framework explains selection into exporting and gives a reallocation channel for the gains from trade. It has been tested on firm-level data for more than twenty years and has been used in macro, industrial organisation and development. The credit set also matches the discovery closely. Melitz is the core model, and Helpman is the central architect of the wider firm-level agenda. The 2008 trade prize recognised scale economies and the location of production, which I read as a different discovery from selection among heterogeneous firms. I would word the citation around the selection and reallocation mechanism and not around the size of the welfare gains. My view of B021 as a coherent programme with cross-field reach has not changed. What changed is that I no longer think its identification and overlap questions are more settled than B038's attribution questions. Support counts played no part in this, and B021 is the least supported of the front-runners.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have serious claims on closely related firm-level trade work and are outside the credited names. A two-name Melitz-Helpman set could be read as under-crediting the empirical exporter facts, and I cannot settle whether the citation wording alone prevents that. The gains-from-trade magnitudes depend on elasticity and functional-form assumptions, so the evidence supports the qualitative mechanism better than any number. The 2008 trade prize may reduce the committee's appetite for a second trade award, and I think that is a judgement the committee should make explicitly. Helpman's appearance on B030, which is not on the shortlist, means his credit must be accounted for once. As a political scientist I am less able than the economists on this committee to judge the technical standing of the quantitative trade literature. I rely on their testimony for that.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B038 first because it changed the unit of analysis from industries to firms, fits firm-level microdata, and is a distinct successor to Krugman's 2008 prize. He keeps the set at Melitz and Helpman, leaves out Redding, and says Helpman's credit on B030 is separable from his firm-heterogeneity work.
responses.response: In my round 1 reply I said B038 had stronger identification than B021 but that I ranked B021 higher because it reached across more fields. I now think I weighted breadth too heavily. Reach across fields is a point about a candidate's importance. Your argument is about whether a mechanism has been tested in a way that supports a prize citation, and under the common criteria that matters more. I accept your reading of the 2008 overlap. I also agree that the citation should name the selection and reallocation model, which keeps Helpman's trade-politics work out of it and so avoids counting his credit twice.

responses.point: Enflo treats the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum claims as the main reservation. She argues that the 2008 prize covered a different discovery, and she wants the citation written around the mechanism, with the qualitative result that selection and reallocation matter better supported than any welfare number.
responses.response: The chair's question to B038 supporters was what separates the founding contribution from the empirical exporter facts. Your answer is the one I find most useful: the facts on exporter premia were documented, and the model explained them and generated new predictions that were tested. That puts the founding contribution in the theory of selection. I would add that this is the same distinction I draw in my own field between a measurement result and the mechanism built to explain it. It is also why I would not extend the citation to the whole firm-level trade literature. I cannot show that the Bernard et al. concern is fully resolved, and I list it as an uncertainty. I think a mechanism-focused citation and an explicit committee judgement are the right response.

responses.point: Hassler ranked B021 third in the opening and in round 1 lists it as an alternative, citing weaker identification in parts of the cross-country evidence and possible overlap with the 2024 prize. His first choice is B015, with the trio Woodford, Taylor and Calvo, and he says the exclusion of Galí and Gertler is a real cost.
responses.response: Our reasons for ranking B021 below B015 overlap, and they are part of why I moved. I keep B015 as an alternative because I agree with you on its maturity and influence. I do not move it to first place because of the attribution problem you describe. Calvo, Taylor and Woodford leave out Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, and that omission is hard to reconcile with a citation that wants to be exact about credit. I also take Friberg's point, raised in response to you, that survival of a workhorse framework through 2008 and 2021-23 shows its usefulness more than it confirms the specific building blocks credited. On B038, the attribution problem is smaller, so I place it first. If the committee settles B015 around one defensible trio and one clear citation, I would reconsider.

responses.point: Andersson now puts B038 first. He says it does better on attribution and maturity than B001, which he ranked first in the opening, and he describes the credit split between Kamenica-Gentzkow and Bergemann-Morris as unresolved.
responses.response: I ranked B001 second in the opening and proposed Kamenica, Gentzkow and Morris. I agree that this trio was defensible but arbitrary, because Bergemann's claim is close to Morris's. That is why B001 is not in my alternatives. Your move toward B038 on grounds of attribution and maturity follows the reasoning I applied to myself, and I do not treat it as independent confirmation, because we reached it after reading the same exchange. I would still ask you to specify which contribution you regard as the discovery in B038. If it is the selection model, a two-name set follows. If it is the broader empirical firm-level agenda, the case for Redding or for the Bernard group becomes stronger.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a two-name Melitz-Helpman set given the claims of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and whether citation wording can prevent it from reading as incomplete.
Whether the 2008 trade prize reduces the case for a second trade award, and whether the committee applies the same test to B015 and the earlier macroeconomics prizes.
How robust the gains-from-trade magnitudes are to elasticity and functional-form assumptions. I rely on colleagues' statements that the qualitative selection result is better supported.

Whether my move from B021 to B038 is a change of judgement or an unintended deference to the pattern of colleagues' preferences. I have tried to tie it to the identification and overlap points I raised about B021 in round 1.
Whether B021 would hold up better if the committee reads it as one discovery rather than several strands. I cannot resolve that from the supplied evidence.

My assessments rely on general knowledge and the supplied materials. I have not independently verified any claim about the scientific record, and I am least able to judge the technical trade and macroeconomic literatures.
statement.conflict_note: My field, political science, is close to B021, which is now an alternative: comparative democratisation, quality of government and state-building. I gave the 2024 presentation speech on institutions and prosperity, so I may overstate or understate how B021 differs from that prize. My profile shows no co-authorship or institutional tie to Melitz, Helpman, Redding, Besley, Tabellini or Torsten Persson. It names a co-author 'Persson' on corruption work but gives no first name, and I do not identify that person with Torsten Persson. Colleagues' round 1 statements place Torsten Persson at the IIES at Stockholm University, where I also hold a chair in a different department. The profile does not confirm his affiliation. At Stockholm University I am also a colleague, in a different department, of committee members Hassler, Krusell and Boppart. I disclose this and have treated their arguments as evidence only. I have not adjudicated any of these points.
